scenes.visual: Title card: Slower Worsening Is Still Worsening.

scenes.tts: A drug clears amyloid from the brain. Does that help the person whose brain it is?
scenes.visual: An amyloid plaque between neurons dissolves as antibody shapes bind it. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: A drug clears amyloid from the brain. Does that help the person whose brain it is?

scenes.tts: The antibody leh-KAN-eh-mab clears amyloid plaques. In a large trial, people with early Alzheimer disease got it or a placebo.
scenes.caption: The antibody lecanemab clears amyloid plaques. In a large trial, people with early Alzheimer disease got it or a placebo.
scenes.visual: Two groups of figures, labelled lecanemab and placebo. On screen only: Clarity AD, 1,795 people, mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia, amyloid confirmed.
scenes.narration: The antibody lecanemab clears amyloid plaques. In a large trial, people with early Alzheimer disease got it or a placebo.

scenes.tts: Both groups were followed for a year and a half.
scenes.visual: A time axis from 0 to 18 months appears along the bottom.
scenes.narration: Both groups were followed for a year and a half.

scenes.tts: The outcome was a clinician's rating of thinking and daily function. It runs from zero to eighteen, and higher means worse. The graph shows each group's change from its starting score.
scenes.visual: A vertical scale bar 0 to 18, arrow upward marked: higher = worse. It slides aside, and the graph's vertical axis appears, labelled: change in CDR-SB from start (points; up = worse), starting at zero change.
scenes.narration: The outcome was a clinician's rating of thinking and daily function. It runs from zero to eighteen, and higher means worse. The graph shows each group's change from its starting score.

scenes.tts: Here is a question. Did the treated group get better?
scenes.visual: Both groups start at zero change on the graph. On screen: Pause. Did the treated group get better?
scenes.narration: Here is a question. Did the treated group get better?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen.

scenes.tts: No. Both lines rise. Both groups got worse. The treated group got worse more slowly.
scenes.visual: Two lines rise from zero change over 18 months: placebo ends at +1.66, lecanemab at +1.21, both labelled on screen. Small label: schematic lines; measured endpoints at 18 months. The gap between the ends is shaded.
scenes.narration: No. Both lines rise. Both groups got worse. The treated group got worse more slowly.

scenes.tts: To compare them, take the gap as a share of the placebo group's decline.
scenes.visual: The placebo rise is drawn as a vertical bar. The shaded gap is lifted beside it.
scenes.narration: To compare them, take the gap as a share of the placebo group's decline.

scenes.tts: The gap is a little more than a quarter of the placebo decline. That share is called the relative slowing.
scenes.visual: The bar splits into a large part and a smaller part. On screen only: 0.45 ÷ 1.66 ≈ 0.27, about 27% relative slowing.
scenes.narration: The gap is a little more than a quarter of the placebo decline. That share is called the relative slowing.

scenes.tts: That share compares two amounts of decline. It is not a gain in memory. It is not the share of patients helped. It is not anyone's prognosis.
scenes.visual: Three crossed-out cards appear: gain in memory; share of patients helped; prognosis. One card stays: compares two amounts of decline.
scenes.narration: That share compares two amounts of decline. It is not a gain in memory. It is not the share of patients helped. It is not anyone's prognosis.

scenes.tts: Slower worsening is still worsening. In this trial, a drug that clears amyloid slowed the disease. It did not stop it.
scenes.visual: Back to the two rising lines (schematic); both end above zero. Label: treated group still worsened.
scenes.narration: Slower worsening is still worsening. In this trial, a drug that clears amyloid slowed the disease. It did not stop it.

scenes.visual: The two lines and the label hold on screen.

scenes.tts: A second trial tested a different antibody, sol-an-EZ-oo-mab. It enrolled older adults whose thinking was still normal, but whose brains held extra amyloid.
scenes.caption: A second trial tested a different antibody, solanezumab. It enrolled older adults whose thinking was still normal, but whose brains held extra amyloid.
scenes.visual: New panel. A group of figures labelled cognitively unimpaired, ages 65 to 85, elevated amyloid. On screen only: A4 study, solanezumab, 240 weeks.
scenes.narration: A second trial tested a different antibody, solanezumab. It enrolled older adults whose thinking was still normal, but whose brains held extra amyloid.

scenes.tts: On pet scans, amyloid rose in both groups. It rose more slowly with the drug.
scenes.caption: On PET scans, amyloid rose in both groups. It rose more slowly with the drug.
scenes.visual: Two amyloid PET lines, both rising; the drug line rises less. Small label: schematic trajectories; numbers are measured 240-week changes. On screen only: +11.6 vs +19.3 centiloids, about 40% smaller increase.
scenes.narration: On PET scans, amyloid rose in both groups. It rose more slowly with the drug.

scenes.tts: Predict. Did their thinking decline more slowly too?
scenes.visual: An empty cognition panel appears beside the PET panel. On screen: Pause. Did thinking decline more slowly?
scenes.narration: Predict. Did their thinking decline more slowly too?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen.

scenes.tts: Both groups declined. The trial did not demonstrate slower decline with the drug, despite the smaller rise in amyloid.
scenes.visual: Two cognition bars, both pointing downward from zero. Label: both groups declined; no statistically significant slowing demonstrated.
scenes.narration: Both groups declined. The trial did not demonstrate slower decline with the drug, despite the smaller rise in amyloid.

scenes.tts: A L S shows the same thing. In people with S O D one A L S, a drug called toe-FER-sen lowered S O D one. It also lowered a blood marker of axon damage.
scenes.caption: ALS shows the same thing. In people with SOD1 ALS, a drug called tofersen lowered SOD1. It also lowered a blood marker of axon damage.
scenes.visual: New panel, labelled: SOD1-mutant ALS. An antisense strand icon labelled tofersen. Two bars fall: SOD1 in spinal fluid, neurofilament light in plasma.
scenes.narration: ALS shows the same thing. In people with SOD1 ALS, a drug called tofersen lowered SOD1. It also lowered a blood marker of axon damage.

scenes.tts: But over twenty-eight weeks, the clinical measures did not improve.
scenes.visual: A card replaces the bars: At 28 weeks, clinical benefit not shown.
scenes.narration: But over twenty-eight weeks, the clinical measures did not improve.

scenes.tts: That is the treatment question. A marker can guide you. But a clinical outcome is what tells you whether changing the target helps.
scenes.visual: The three cards from chapter one appear; the third card, Does changing it help? (randomized trials in people), glows.
scenes.narration: That is the treatment question. A marker can guide you. But a clinical outcome is what tells you whether changing the target helps.

scenes.tts: Benefits also have costs. Another antibody, doe-NAN-eh-mab, was tested in a large trial. Brain swelling or fluid on M R I was far more common with it than on placebo.
scenes.caption: Benefits also have costs. Another antibody, donanemab, was tested in a large trial. Brain swelling or fluid on MRI was far more common with it than on placebo.
scenes.visual: An MRI icon with a highlighted patch. On screen only: ARIA with edema or effusion, donanemab 24.0% vs placebo 2.1%.
scenes.narration: Benefits also have costs. Another antibody, donanemab, was tested in a large trial. Brain swelling or fluid on MRI was far more common with it than on placebo.

scenes.visual: The MRI panel and the two lecanemab lines hold side by side.

scenes.tts: Read a trial as two amounts of decline. And keep a change in a marker apart from a change in the person.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: two amounts of decline; a marker is not the person.
scenes.narration: Read a trial as two amounts of decline. And keep a change in a marker apart from a change in the person.
